description: Assist mode: the Playwright-grade MCP server (stdio) that is a SUPERSET of Playwright MCP and works STANDALONE with NO model weights present. Owns the ref/snapshot boundary in-house (no dependency on Playwright's private _snapshotForAI, which was VERIFIED absent in stable 1.63.0). Implements the browser lifecycle, the ref-assigning accessibility snapshot, and the familiar tools. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: src/browser.ts: a BrowserSession wrapper around Playwright chromium. Config: headless (default true) / headed, viewport, optional channel. Lazily launches a browser + context + page. Exposes getPage(), close(), and a resolveRef(ref: Ref) helper that returns a Locator via page.locator('[data-laya-ref="<ref>"]') and, if the target string is not a known ref, treats it as a raw Playwright selector (Boundary Discipline: parse/guard the target at this boundary).

src/snapshot.ts: capture(page) that injects an in-page script (page.evaluate) walking the DOM for interactive + landmark elements (a, button, input, textarea, select, [role], [contenteditable], headings, labels), assigning each a stable data-laya-ref='eN' attribute (monotonic per snapshot), and returning both (a) a compact human-readable YAML-ish snapshot string with lines like '- button "Search" [ref=e5]' and current values for inputs, and (b) a Control[] array (role, name, tag, type, value, options for selects, editable/checked/disabled). Also return url, title, and a truncated visibleText. Reuse this single capture for BOTH Assist snapshot output and Autopilot state building. This is the linchpin — make it robust to detached nodes and re-runnable (idempotent ref assignment per capture).

src/tools/ implement Assist tools registered on the MCP server, each with a zod input schema, mirroring Playwright MCP conventions (params: optional 'element' human-readable description + 'target' ref-or-selector where applicable): browser_navigate({url}); browser_snapshot() -> returns the compact snapshot text; browser_click({element?, target, doubleClick?, button?}); browser_type({element?, target, text, submit?, slowly?}); browser_select_option({element?, target, values:string[]}); browser_press_key({key}); browser_wait_for({text?, textGone?, time?}); browser_close(). Each mutating tool should return a fresh snapshot after acting so the client sees the new state, matching Playwright MCP behavior.

src/server.ts: build the McpServer from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, register all Assist tools, and wire tool handlers to a shared BrowserSession. Advertise the 'sampling' capability requirement note in server info (used later by Autopilot). src/index.ts: the bin entry — construct the server, connect a StdioServerTransport, handle SIGINT/SIGTERM to close the browser. No weights are loaded in Assist mode.

Tests: test/snapshot.test.ts drives a real headless chromium against a local static HTML fixture (test/fixtures/login.html or similar) and asserts the captured Control[] contains the expected refs/roles/names and that resolveRef finds the element. test/assist.test.ts exercises browser_navigate + browser_snapshot + browser_type + browser_click against a fixture served via file:// or an in-process http.Server, asserting literal outcomes (e.g., after clicking submit the URL/hash or a result element changes). Tests must pass with NO model weights present.
acceptance_criteria: The MCP server starts over stdio (node dist/index.js) and lists all eight Assist tools with correct schemas, with no model weights present.
browser_snapshot returns a compact text snapshot where interactive elements carry stable [ref=eN] markers.
A target ref from a snapshot resolves to the correct element and browser_click / browser_type act on it; an unknown target is treated as a raw selector.
test/snapshot.test.ts and test/assist.test.ts pass against local HTML fixtures in headless chromium with no weights.
Assist mode has zero dependency on Playwright's private _snapshotForAI / snapshotForAI.
verification: Run 'pnpm run typecheck' and 'pnpm run build' with zero errors.
Run 'pnpm run test' and confirm the snapshot and assist tests pass in headless chromium.
Optionally boot 'node dist/index.js' and send an MCP list-tools request over stdio to confirm the eight Assist tools are advertised.
findings: Implemented Assist mode fully, standalone with no model weights. Files: src/browser.ts (BrowserSession: lazy chromium launch, headless default, viewport, optional channel, bounded action/nav timeouts of 10s/20s so missing-element actions surface errors promptly instead of hanging 30s; resolveRef treats an 'eN'-shaped target as the data-laya-ref locator and any other string as a raw Playwright selector). src/snapshot.ts (capture() runs a self-contained in-page DOM walk via page.evaluate over a,button,input,textarea,select,[role],[contenteditable],headings,labels; stamps monotonic data-laya-ref='eN'; returns Control[] with role/name/tag/type/value/options/checked/disabled + a compact text snapshot with [ref=eN] markers + url/title/truncated visibleText; re-runnable/idempotent). src/tools/*.ts (eight tools with zod inputSchema: navigate, snapshot, click, type, select_option, press_key, wait_for, close; Playwright-MCP element+target convention; mutating tools return a fresh snapshot; failures return isError text results). src/server.ts (createServer builds McpServer, registers all Assist tools on a shared session, advertises a sampling-capability note in instructions for later Autopilot). src/index.ts (bin entry: StdioServerTransport, SIGINT/SIGTERM close browser+server, logs to stderr to keep stdout JSON-RPC clean). Tests: test/helpers/fixture-server.ts (loopback http static server for fixtures), test/fixtures/login.html, test/snapshot.test.ts, test/assist.test.ts — real headless chromium, no weights, asserting literal outcomes (control refs/roles/names/options, resolveRef by ref and raw selector, form drive changes #status/title/#signed-in hash). DEVIATIONS/NOTES: (1) Added 'DOM','DOM.Iterable' to tsconfig.json lib so the in-page evaluate body type-checks against browser globals (skipLibCheck already on; Node types still available). (2) snapshot skips redundant <label> elements (those with a resolvable for= target or wrapping a field) so a field's name is not duplicated by a bare label control; headings/labels with no name are dropped. (3) The 'matches nothing' error test takes ~10s (waits the 10s action timeout) — well under the 30s vitest timeout. VERIFIED: no dependency on Playwright private _snapshotForAI/snapshotForAI or ariaSnapshot [ref] markers. All green: pnpm run typecheck, pnpm run build, pnpm run test (14 tests, 3 files). Booted node dist/index.js over stdio and confirmed tools/list advertises all eight Assist tools with correct schemas and clean SIGTERM shutdown.
